brief: Deutsche Bank Research Institute's September chartbook argues the yield rise is normalisation, not stress. US nominal GDP at 6.6% year on year sits about 180bps above the 10-year Treasury yield, so on that gap yields are not high, and the bank puts fair value at 4.8% if nominal growth settles at 5.5% or around 5.3% if it settles at 6%. Higher coupons mean Treasury and gilt total return indices are up even as yields approach highs. On the Fed, core PCE sits 15bps off a 34-year high, trend inflation is near 3%, ISM services prices paid is at a 4-year high, financial conditions are the loosest since 1990 and payrolls have trended up in 2026, so the 2025 insurance cuts look ripe to be reversed. Deutsche Bank economists expect an ECB hike this week and another to 2.75% in December after the energy shock pushed the real deposit rate negative. Q2 brought the strongest non-pandemic global earnings expansion on record, AI capex is concentrated in five hyperscalers now issuing rather than buying back stock, and leadership has rotated away from the Mag-7. Japan is flagged on a 40-year-low yen and 15.4tn yen of intervention.
